text: The difference between the contractors gave p = 0.03, so there is a 3% chance that the two contractors are really the same.
District D07 showed no significant change (p = 0.40), which proves that the new valve schedule has no effect there.
If the two contractors truly had the same satisfaction, a difference at least as large as the one we observed would turn up in about 3 studies in 100.
With p = 0.001 the effect of the reminder message is large and worth rolling out.
The 95% interval for the mean repair time is 8.1 to 9.6 hours, so 95% of repairs take between 8.1 and 9.6 hours.
We used a 95% method: across many studies run this way, about 95 in 100 of the intervals it produces would contain the true mean.
We tested all 30 districts at the 0.05 level and found two significant ones, so each of the two findings has only a 5% chance of being a false alarm.
The standard error of the mean consumption, 4.1 litres, describes how far a sample mean of this size typically lands from the population mean.
